Model review · October 17, 2026

Why Google shows $167.71

The original result reproduces correctly. Its main driver is a cautious growth and reinvestment path. A more flexible forecast is useful; a $250 minimum is not a validation test.

June 2026 TTM financial reference · USD per common share · Educational conditional valuation

No material arithmetic error or wrong-issuer input was found in the items checked. The 18% growth input means year one, then an immediate fade to 2.5% in year ten. That produces a 10.14% revenue CAGR. The specialist claims overlay actually adds $10.10 per share versus a simple cash-minus-debt bridge.

The source checks

Revenue reconciles to $445.866bn and operating income to $147.628bn using annual + current six months − prior-year six months. The starting margin is 33.1104%, without an EBIT adjustment. See the FY2025 statements and Q2 filing.

The unusual preferred securities are genuine Alphabet instruments. The Series A and Series B certificates support the conversion inputs. The June balance sheet and notes reconcile the cash, debt, investments, finance leases and noncontrolling interests; noncurrent investments do not duplicate current marketables. The separate August debt issuance is outside this dated capital reference.

The model deducts $114.65bn of net reinvestment from $134.60bn year-one NOPAT, leaving $19.95bn FCFF. Terminal operations account for 67.4% of operating enterprise value. Depreciation inside EBIT plus net reinvestment is not a double deduction of gross capex.

Cautious judgments, not incorrect facts

  • 18% growth: below the latest quarter's 24%. The exact immediate fade has less company-specific support than a separate near-term Services/Cloud forecast. Issuer results
  • 30% mature margin: assumes erosion from 33.11%. It is a scenario, not an established destination. Maintaining the starting margin alone gives $183.38.
  • 0.70x sales/capital: expensive growth, but within the order of magnitude of the recent buildout. A constant decade-long ratio needs stronger justification. Raising it to 1.00x alone gives $184.12.
  • 10% WACC: the worksheet is internally correct. The observed ten-year Treasury yield is 5.09%; beta, risk premium, debt weight and spread are assumptions. Using the unrounded 9.76771% gives $173.68. At 9%: $196.59; at 8%: $236.47.

These are one-factor sensitivities on the original path. They are not additive. Removing every cautious input would create an optimistic scenario rather than demonstrate a correction.

Three or five explicit years, then a fade

Hold 18% growth through the explicit period, then fade to 2.5% in the selected maturity year. Margin fades to 30% over the full horizon. Taxes, WACC, terminal ROIC and claims remain unchanged.

Constant capital retains 0.70x sales/capital. Consistent capital holds it through the explicit period, then fades its reciprocal to terminal intensity. For this case, terminal sales/capital is 0.6253908693x, so consistency slightly lowers value.

For year y, explicit period E and maturity N: t = max(0, (y − E) / (N − E)). Capital intensity = (1 − t) / 0.7 + t × (1 + g) × mature margin × (1 − tax) / terminal ROIC.

The five-year/20-year case is a conditional $260.74. It also requires 9.10 times starting revenue and $5.42tn cumulative net reinvestment. Longer horizons change the business forecast; choose them using operating evidence, not the desired share value.

What still needs care

  • Investment carrying values are gross proxies before realization taxes and liquidity discounts. Employee awards and the preferred payoff are not fully appraised. No capped-call recovery is credited.
  • The result uses June capital. It is not a live October balance sheet or market quote.
  • Any adjustment for legal charges must also address settlement cash, taxes and double-counting. Lease/funding commitments must agree with the operating forecast.
  • A genuine, tiny documentation mismatch remains: the research dividend PV uses ACT/365, while runtime uses ACT/365.25. The difference is $0.00001622 per share, not the valuation gap.

Reproducible calculation: full-precision JSON and annual cash flows. In the repository, run node scripts/audit-goog-valuation.mjs. The oracle imports no production valuation functions and checks both the original result and terminal FCFF continuity. Full audit: GOOG-VALUATION-AUDIT.md.
